samples.summary: Pasted-HTML `href` is stored without a scheme allowlist, and this change makes such hrefs sticky (Clear formatting no longer strips them)
samples.evidence: Vector: attacker gets a victim (or a collaborator on a shared doc) to paste crafted HTML containing `<a href="javascript:...">` / `data:text/html` / `file:` — `parseHtmlToBlocks` copies the attribute verbatim into `style.href` (packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:610-613 and the duplicate walk at :712-715), and the clipboard-payload sanitizer accepts any string too (`sanitizeInlineStyle`, clipboard.ts:148-149). Nothing validates the scheme at ingest; every *consumer* validates instead (`text-editor.ts:1822`, `text-editor.ts:2176`, `docs-link-popover.tsx:217/224`, `pdf-painter.ts:903`, `serialize/markdown.ts:384`, slides `import/pptx/text.ts:567`). Before this diff, `CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE` containing `href: undefined` (types.ts:315, removed here) gave a user one bulk action that scrubbed such hrefs off a whole selection; after it, the unsafe value persists in the CRDT indefinitely (backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:94 replicates it to every collaborator). I could not complete an exploit chain — I found no ungated href consumer — so this is a hardening finding, not a live XSS: the risk is that the ingest point stays permissive and the next consumer added (an HTML export, a share preview, a mobile renderer) inherits a stored `javascript:` payload. Suggested hardening: gate at ingest with the existing `isSafeUrl` in clipboard.ts:610/712 and clipboard.ts:148, so unsafe schemes never enter the document model.
searchedFor: Grep `href` across packages/docs/src (11 files, all read at the href sites)
Grep `CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE` across packages/**/*.{ts,tsx} to check for allowlist/keyset reuse

samples.summary: After this change the only href-removal path is caret-scoped `removeLink`, so there is no bulk way to strip links from a selection
samples.evidence: `removeLink` resolves a single link run at the caret (`findLinkRunAt(block, cursor.position.offset)`, text-box-editor.ts:1234-1244; the docs `EditorAPI.removeLink` behaves the same, which the new test acknowledges by parking the caret at offset 6 before calling it — editor-clear-formatting.test.ts). With `href` removed from `CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE`, a user who has pasted untrusted content containing many links (possibly tracking or unsafe-scheme URLs) must place the caret inside each one individually; there is no selection-wide remediation action. This is a remediation-ergonomics gap rather than a vulnerability — the design decision to keep links through Clear formatting is defensible (it matches Word) — but a selection-scoped `removeLink` would restore the bulk scrub the diff removes.
